take_homes: An agent's review of its own work is too kind. Check it against what I know, or get a cold second reader that sees only the output.
Put what I learn into a rules file and sharpen it each round (work, capture, reflect, sharpen), so a fresh agent can reuse it.
Generic output usually means my context is thin. Add one sharp, true detail instead of rewording the prompt.

monday.move: Write a context and rules file for the usage-pricing brief, run it with a cold-critic pass, then draft the module-2-start handoff note.
monday.who: Me first, then one person from my team of fourteen to see whether they can pick it up.
monday.stop_condition: The cold reader still flags generic claims after one added detail, or the file only works if I explain it.
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for context files, so each person would keep their own copy.

misconception.why: The durable value was a rules file a fresh agent reuses, plus the cold-read check, not a cleverer prompt. I still think prompt wording matters somewhat, so it is shaken and not changed.

one_line: Good bones: the look-back, the rules file and the cold read earn their hour. The same filler paragraph shows up about ten times, and the module needs that cut.
